title: align-connector-heartbeat-adaptive-backoff-typed-stream-surface
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce cross-SDK connector heartbeat (optional), new jittered exponential retry profiles for streaming, and a simplified typed stream consumer surface. Bumps SDK package versions: python 0.22.0, typescript 2.8.0, go 1.5.0. No behavioral breaking changes when feature flags are off.
description:
Context and motivation: production customers reported intermittent long-tail stream stalls when upstream routing briefly failed or when idle connections were reclaimed by intermediate NAT timeouts. Different SDKs had slightly divergent approaches: TS refreshed tokens on different timers, Go relied on TCP keepalive defaults, and Python had a separate health ping implementation. This PR harmonizes a cross-sdk connector heartbeat and a small ergonomic typed stream surface, and standardizes an adaptive, jittered backoff profile for streaming reconnects.

Goals (high level):
- Provide an opt-in connector heartbeat on long-lived stream connections to improve server-side detection and faster failover when routing changes occur.
- Standardize a jittered exponential backoff profile shared by all SDKs to reduce thundering herd reconnections and improve SLOs.
- Offer a simpler typed stream consumer surface that centralizes cancel/resume semantics across Python/TS/Go.
- Bump SDK versions and update CHANGELOGs.

What changed (summary of commits):
- Add connector/heartbeat logic to runtime client library (lib/connector/heartbeat.*).
- Implement jittered backoff profiles and configs (sdk/common/backoff_profiles.go / py / ts).
- Introduce StreamHandle / TypedStreamConsumer abstractions for each SDK to unify cancel, pause, resume, and health checks.
- Add opt-in feature flagging and env var knobs (REDWOOD_SDK_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS, REDWOOD_SDK_HEARTBEAT_TTL_MS).
- Docs: update quickstarts and examples across redwood-quickstarts and SDK docs with code samples.
- Tests: E2E streaming tests updated to cover heartbeat behavior and reconnection profiles.

Files touched (high level):
- sdk/common/backoff_profiles.go (new)
- sdk/ts/src/stream/typed_consumer.ts (new)
- sdk/py/redwood/stream/typed_consumer.py (new)
- runtime/connector/heartbeat.go (new)
- docs/sdk/heartbeat.md (new)
- redwood-quickstarts/streaming-heartbeat/example-usage.ts (updated)
- ci/e2e/streaming-heartbeat.yml (updated)
- CHANGELOGs and package.json / setup.py bumps

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation for all three SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
- [x] Shared config/feature-flag implementation
- [x] Unit tests for backoff and heartbeat logic
- [x] E2E tests covering reconnect and idle reclaim scenarios
- [x] Documentation and quickstart updates
- [x] Version bumps and CHANGELOG entries

Review conversation (high level extract):
- Diego: "Can we make the heartbeat opt-in by default and expose both interval and ttl? Also request tests for NAT timeout scenario."
  - Aisha: "Yes — default is off. Added env var knobs and new e2e that simulates NAT timeout via idle timeouts in the harness."
- Lina: "TS linter flagged some types; please ensure API surface matches the other SDKs (cancel/resume naming)."
  - Aisha: "Adjusted names to TypedStreamConsumer.{cancel,resume,healthCheck} and added deprecation notes for old methods in the TS adapter."
- Tomáš: "Go: consider syscall-level keepalive interactions on Linux; we should avoid overriding system keepalive unless explicitly configured."
  - Aisha: "We kept system defaults and use the heartbeat as an application-level layer; added docs and comments."
- CI: initial run failed on TS lint and one flaky e2e. Fixed linting and increased e2e test timeout, re-ran and green.

CI checks (timeline):
1) GitHub Actions: build (pass), unit tests (pass), lint (fail on TS types) — fixed in commit 3, re-run passed.
2) E2E: streaming suite initial run failed on a simulated high-latency job — adjusted harness and re-ran. Final: pass.
3) Security scan: pass.

Compatibility notes:
- Heartbeat is disabled by default; enabling it should not change normal request/response behavior.
- Backoff profile values are conservative (defaults chosen to avoid additional cost).
- Typing surface is additive; deprecated wrappers remain for one release cycle.

Telemetry and observability:
- Added two metrics: sdk.connector.heartbeat_sent and sdk.connector.heartbeat_missed.
- Added an event log when a reconnect is triggered by a missed heartbeat to aid post-mortem.

Performance:
- Microbenchmarks show <0.5% median token latency impact when heartbeat is enabled at a 30s interval; documented in docs/perf/heartbeat.md.

Merge notes: squash-and-merge. Post-merge actions: publish SDK packages (py/ts/go) and coordinate a small announcement to customers using Dedicated and Private channels.

Related work: ENG-3189 (streaming reliability), ENG-3204 (sdk ergonomics).
